turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must say, Your Majesty, that your presence here is a great concern, and I am eager to understand the nature of the problem that brings you to our humble abode.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must caution you, Your Majesty, that the matter you seek to discuss with me is likely to be of a highly sensitive and confidential nature.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear that I have brought danger to this esteemed household, gentlemen, and for that, I am eternally grateful for your discretion.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I see you have taken the liberty of trusting me, Your Majesty. Now, let us proceed with all due haste, that we may unravel the tangled threads of your problem.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I am intrigued, Your Majesty, and I must admit that I sense a great weight of concern in your words. Might I request a brief explanation of the nature of this problem, that we may better understand the gravity of the situation?

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Very well, Your Majesty, I shall ask the questions. Tell me, what is the nature of the influence you suspect may have an impact on European history?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must confess, Messieurs, that the matter which weighs upon my mind is one of great import, and I fear that the consequences of inaction would be catastrophic, not only for my own person, but for the stability of Europe itself.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Tell me, Your Majesty, what is the nature of the information that you fear may compromise your interests and, by extension, those of Europe?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must be cautious, Messieurs, for I fear that I have walked into a trap, and that my own actions may have inadvertently led to the discovery of a certain...indiscretion.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must insist, Your Majesty, that you reveal the nature of this indiscretion, that we may better understand the full extent of the situation and the potential consequences of inaction.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I fear, Messieurs, that my sister, Irene Adler, may be in possession of information that could bring ruin to my house and compromise the alliances I have worked so hard to maintain. I beg of you, you must find a way to prevent her from using this knowledge to her advantage.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must warn you, Your Majesty, that your sister's reputation precedes her. She is a woman of intelligence and cunning, and I fear that she may not be as easily swayed as you hope.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must say, Your Majesty, that I am intrigued by the mention of your sister, Irene Adler. Her reputation is certainly formidable, but I wonder, is there not another way to approach this situation, rather than relying solely on my friend Sherlock's exceptional abilities?

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must say, Dr. Watson's skepticism is quite warranted, considering the subject at hand. The King of Bohemia's sister, Irene Adler, is a woman of singular abilities and I suspect she will not be easily intimidated by my...facilities. I suggest we proceed with caution and gather as much information as possible before making any further moves.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I implore you, Messieurs, to consider the gravity of the situation. My sister's...indiscretion could topple the delicate balance of power in Europe, and I fear for the future of my kingdom.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must warn you, Your Majesty, that we cannot simply rush into this situation without a thorough understanding of the circumstances. I require more information about the nature of your sister's...indiscretion and the specifics of the information she may possess.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I must confess, Messieurs, that my sister's actions are...complicated. She has been involved with a most unsavory character, and I fear that her reputation will be irreparably damaged if this matter becomes public.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: I must admit, Your Majesty, that I am beginning to understand the gravity of the situation. However, I still believe that there may be a diplomatic way to resolve this matter, one that does not require the...unconventional methods of my friend Sherlock here.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: I beg of you, Messieurs, to understand the weight of my desperation. My sister's actions, though...distasteful, are but a symptom of a greater problem, one that threatens to engulf my kingdom and plunge Europe into chaos.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: I must admit, Your Majesty, that I find your sister's situation to be a classic case of a tangled web of deceit and misaligned interests. I require a list of all parties involved, including the unsavory character you mentioned, and the specific information your sister possesses.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: I told you that I would call.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: Pray take a seat. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases. Whom have I the honour to address?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman. I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance. If not, I should much prefer to communicate with you alone.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: It is both, or none. You may say before this gentleman anything which you may say to me.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Then I must begin, by binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance. At present it is not too much to say that it is of such weight it may have an influence upon European history.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You will excuse this mask. The august person who employs me wishes his agent to be unknown to you, and I may confess at once that the title by which I have just called myself is not exactly my own.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: The circumstances are of great delicacy, and every precaution has to be taken to quench what might grow to be an immense scandal and seriously compromise one of the reigning families of Europe. To speak plainly, the matter implicates the great House of Ormstein, hereditary kings of Bohemia.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: I was also aware of that

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Our visitor glanced with some apparent surprise at the languid, lounging figure of the man who had been no doubt depicted to him as the most incisive reasoner and most energetic agent in Europe. Holmes slowly reopened his eyes and looked impatiently at his gigantic client.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: If your Majesty would condescend to state your case, I should be better able to advise you.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You are right. I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?
